Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment is a classic AP-MS (Affinity Purification Mass Spectrometry) workflow using immunoprecipitation of MYC/MYCN. While the text mentions polyubiquitination and phosphorylation in the biological results, the mass spectrometry analysis itself was used for interactome identification (AP-MS) and not for PTM-site mapping or enrichment of remnants (e.g., diGly). PRIDE metadata explicitly states 'No PTMs are included in the dataset'.

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The mass spectrometry experiment described in the text and PRIDE metadata is an affinity purification (AP-MS) study to identify interactors of MYC and MYCN. While the broader paper explores perturbations (EZH2 depletion, inhibitors), the specific MS analysis was performed on baseline cellular extracts from Kelly and NCI-H2171 cells to map the interactome. Therefore, this is not a differential perturbation study in the context of the MS data; it is a descriptive interactome analysis comparing IP vs IgG control.
